newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan public funds seen investing 10 trillion yen.
newsitem.headline: Japan public funds seen investing 10 trillion yen.

text.p: Japanese public bodies are expected to invest some 10 trillion yen in domestic and overseas financial markets in the 1997/98 fiscal year which began on April 1, economists said on Friday.
The Pension Welfare Service Public Corp, an affiliate of the Health and Welfare Ministry, is expected to invest about one trillion yen in 1997/98.
The Postal Life Insurance Welfare Service Public Corp, an affiliate of the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry, is expected to be 1.65 trillion yen, they said.
The Posts and Telecommunications Ministry, also invests in the markets through two of its units, the Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo) and the Postal Savings Bureau (Yucho).
Fresh investment by the two institutions is likely to total about eight trillion yen in 1997/98, they said.
An economist at Daiwa Institute of Research said a maximum of some 2.8 trillion yen worth of new public fund money could be invested in Japanese stocks this fiscal year.
If the investment pattern is the same this year as in recent years, about half of the 2.8 trillion yen is expected to be placed during April to June, he said.
In order to minimise investment risks, stock transactions by public bodies' are more strictly regulated than their investment in foreign and domestic bonds. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8570
